one_line: 克利夫兰美术馆藏画作，馆方断代作「1360」。**本条为著录级**：照录馆方记录，未作阐释。

colophons.text:
至正廿年春正月_日作此併系鄙語于尾

地偏人遠閉柴關，滿院松陰白晝閒。
眼底風塵渾忘却，坐看流水臥看山。

吳興姚廷美畫

馆方英译：Artist's inscription, poem, and signature: 

In the first month of spring in the twentieth year of the reign of Zhizheng [1360], I painted this and attached a few rustic words at the end of the scroll. 

A secluded place, one may close the thatch door. 
In a courtyard fully shaded by pines, a moment of daytime leisure awaits. 
Sights of wind and dust can be utterly forgotten. 
One sits to view the cascades, or lies down [better] to see the hills.

Painted by Yao Tingmei of Wuxing

Colophon by Yang Weizhen, "An Essay on Leisure to Spare":

Master Ouyang [Ouyang Xiu, 1007–1072] says in one of his poems, "To have good company is such a joy. It provides the rare excuse to steal away leisure from one's life." Now, if leisure could be acquired only by stealing, this certainly could not be said to be abundant enough to spare. In the poetry of Su Dongpo [1036–1101] he says, "It is indeed not bad to be able to secure leisure because of illness." Now if leisure should have been obtained from an illness that is against one's wish, this again could not be said to be abundant enough to spare. How vulgar is the poem by a man of late Sung who talks about buying plenty of farm and homestead land in preparation for the coming days of leisure. Now, if leisure has to depend on the extensive holding of real estate, this is precisely the kind of thing which will jeopardize one's leisure. Indeed, one will never have enough leisure that way, let alone enough to spare.

In Qinglong by the Song River, there is a hermit, Mr. Tu. Inside, he has fine children to take care of his household. Under him, he has diligent servants to engage in production. Outside, he has wise relatives and friends to watch out and guard him. Thus he has been able to live peacefully, and to eat heartily, and to pass his time in rest and play. Surely his leisure was not stolen from the few moments when he has company. It was not derived from illness. It was not jeopardized by extensive holdings of real estate. Could anyone question my word if I said this is truly abundant enough to spare? Mr. Tu asked a common friend, Zhang Mengchen, to come to me for an essay. I herewith composed this for him as above. At the same time, others who are well versed in poetry have written poems as in the following.

Dong wei zi wrote this on the first day of the second month of the gengzi year [1360]. By "Dong wei" I mean the jinshi graduate from the examination in the dingmao year of Taiding [1327], with the present rank of Feng xun dai fu, and in the office of Commissioner of Schools for the Jiangxi and other provinces, whose name is Yang Weizhen.

Signed Gongchen 拱辰
